provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Mechanism: square holes in the scatter are filled, largest first. The background is palette[0] and the fill colour is palette[1]. For each square size s, from min(H,W) down to 2, the program finds every s×s window that is entirely background in the current grid and paints it with the fill colour. Painted cells are no longer background, so smaller squares only fill space that is still empty. The generator computes all valid windows of one size at once, stamps them, and rejects any scene where windows of the same size overlap. So in valid scenes the windows of each size are pairwise disjoint, and the result does not depend on scan order. That makes the procedure D4-invariant: the same direct-coordinate scan works under every rotation or reflection without changing any direction. Only the two colour roles are specialised, through the palette. Grey (palette[5]) is simply anything that is not background, and it is left unchanged. Rectangular grids are handled by limiting the window size to min(H,W).
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes the generator's guarantee that same-size all-background windows are disjoint. If an off-domain input breaks that guarantee, overlapping candidates are resolved by visible reading order, which may not match a rotated reference. The background and fill roles come from the palette rather than from the demonstrations. The fixtures are consistent with this uniform rule, and I found no contradictions. I have not run any tests.
